name: gammu
desc: Command-line utility to control a phone
why: Talks to phones over AT commands, serial, and Bluetooth; a real door into old modem-era phone protocols.

brief.what_it_is: Gammu is a command-line utility, written in C and built on libGammu, for controlling a mobile phone. The README says it covers call listing and handling, SMS retrieval, backup and sending, MMS retrieval, phonebook export and import (including vCard), calendar and task export and import (vCalendar or iCalendar), phone and network information, and access to the phone file system. Support varies by phone, and the homepage points to a Gammu Phone Database for per-phone reports. The package also includes the Gammu SMS Daemon, the libGammu library, and Python bindings for building your own applications. The executables in the package are gammu, gammu-config, gammu-detect, gammu-smsd, gammu-smsd-inject, gammu-smsd-monitor, and jadmaker. The homepage and README I read do not mention AT commands, serial, or Bluetooth, so those transports come from the scout notes, not from the pages.
brief.why_it_exists: The project forked from Gnokii and was originally called MyGnokii2 up to version 0.58. The name Gammu was chosen as an acronym for 'Gammu All Mobile Management Utilities' when a better name was needed, and the homepage notes that the author did not know of the Heretics of Dune character.
brief.how_it_works: The command-line tool sits on top of the libGammu C library, which does the phone communication. The package also ships the SMS daemon and Python bindings so other programs can drive a phone through the same library. The pages I read do not describe the transport mechanism in detail.
brief.install_notes: The pages I read give no installation steps beyond downloading the package for your platform. Documentation ships with the program as The Gammu Manual, and the README says an HTML build is available with make manual-html. The source is on GitHub under GPL v2.
brief.standout: It is a long-running, open-source phone-control toolkit with a library, a daemon, and language bindings, not just a single utility. The homepage notes a per-phone compatibility database, which reflects how uneven phone support is across handsets.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage lists Gammu 1.45.1 published Oct. 19, 2026 and Gammu 1.45.0 published Sept. 16, 2026, both from GitHub release automation. The GitHub README says the project is led by Michal Cihar with many contributors, and it links to a translation project and donation page.
brief.caveats: Support depends on the specific phone model, and the homepage says some phones act as USB storage devices and cannot be reached through Gammu. Gammu is GPL v2. I did not see build requirements in the pages I read. I did not verify the AT command, serial, or Bluetooth claims from the scout notes on the pages I fetched.
quotes: Gammu is the name of the project as well as name of command line utility, which you can use to control your phone.
Gammu is library and command line utility for mobile phones. It is released under GNU GPL version 2.
Gammu was chosen as an acronym for Gammu All Mobile Management Utilities, without knowing that Gammu from the "Heretics of Dune" book written by Frank Herbert exists.
